solutions.check: grid rebuilt from the blog's light list (unique); every answer written into it with each crossing agreeing

clue.text: One in seven miners is retiring

definitions.meaning: the seven dwarfs of Snow White mine for gems, and one of them is the shy one
retiring here means shy and self-effacing

explanation.surface: A member of a seven-strong mining crew is about to leave work for good.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Retiring' looks like stopping work, but it means shy; the seven miners are Snow White's dwarfs.
explanation.definitionFit: Retiring in the sense of shy and modest is a dictionary synonym for the dwarf's name.

clue.text: 'Rocky' a bad role inspiring great affection

indicators.note: rocky means shaky or unsteady, so the letters that follow are shaken into a new order

explanation.surface: A film role in Rocky is a poor part yet wins the audience's love.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Rocky' looks like the film title, but it is the anagram signal working on A BAD ROLE.
explanation.definitionFit: Something lovable inspires deep affection, the plain dictionary sense of the word.

clue.text: Close broadcast with no current issue

indicators.note: something broadcast is spoken over the air, so we hear the word rather than see it

parts.note: close weather is stuffy and muggy, lacking fresh air

explanation.surface: Shutting down a transmission leaves no pressing topic to discuss.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Close' is the adjective for muggy weather, not the verb to shut.
explanation.definitionFit: Issue means offspring, so having no current issue means having no child to inherit.

clue.text: Perfect referee to control Northern Ireland and Austria heading for draw

annotationWithheld.why: Perfect referee to control Northern Ireland and Austria heading for draw (10): NI and A go separately into UMPIRE (U-NI-MP-A-IRE) + D; the only parse nests a container as holder of another, which the grammar refuses
annotationWithheld.clue: Perfect referee to control Northern Ireland and Austria heading for draw

clue.text: It's nonsense some characters in Branagh's 'Othello' are upset

indicators.note: in a down clue upset means turned upside down, so the run reads from bottom to top
only a few of the letters of the quoted words are used, running across them

explanation.surface: A critic dismisses parts of Kenneth Branagh's Othello as rubbish that leaves audiences upset.
explanation.walkthrough: The run H-S-O-T across Branagh's Othello, read upward, gives the slang word for rubbish.
explanation.definitionFit: Tosh is British slang for rubbish talk, a direct synonym of nonsense.

clue.text: Temperature or pressure leads to overriding and ruinous inertia

parts.note: taken as written
P is the physics symbol for pressure

indicators.note: the leads of words are their first letters, taken from the two words after

explanation.surface: Heat or stress can cause a crushing, ruinous lethargy.
explanation.definitionFit: Torpor is sluggish inactivity, a close synonym of inertia in its everyday sense.

clue.text: Bound to be hot below opening either side of chimney

indicators.note: in a down clue the hot letter sits below, so it comes last
the opening's letters sit on either side of the chimney, enclosing it

parts.note: a gap is an opening
lum is a Scots word for a chimney
H is the abbreviation for hot, as on taps

explanation.surface: Someone is sure to get hot sitting under a fireplace opening near the chimney.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Bound' looks like 'certain', but it is the leap; LUM is a Scottish dialect word for chimney.
explanation.definitionFit: To galumph is to bound or bounce along clumsily, a word coined by Lewis Carroll.

clue.text: Born in chirpy milieu of East London

indicators.note: in tells us the birth word goes inside the chirpy word

parts.note: cocky means cheeky and chirpy, full of confidence
née, written NE in family trees, is French for born

explanation.surface: Someone was brought up among the cheerful surroundings of East London.
explanation.walkthrough: 'milieu' is a link word here, echoing the idea of surroundings; NE stands for née.
explanation.definitionFit: A cockney is a native of the East End, so the word describes something belonging to East London.

clue.text: State induced by depression or trouble

parts.note: a col is a dip or pass between mountain peaks
taken as written
ado means fuss or trouble

explanation.surface: A mood of the nation brought on by gloom or difficulties.
explanation.walkthrough: 'State' looks like a condition of mind; it is a US state, and 'depression' is geographical.
explanation.definitionFit: Colorado is one of the fifty United States, so it is an example of a state.

clue.text: Sue is so proper

parts.note: taken as written
licit means lawful or proper

explanation.surface: A woman named Sue is a very correct sort of person.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Sue' looks like a woman's name, but it is the verb to petition.
explanation.definitionFit: To sue is to plead or petition for something, which is what soliciting means.

clue.text: Lump welcomes lunchtime — he likes to fill his face

definitions.text: he likes to fill his face

indicators.note: to welcome is to take in, so the lump's letters receive the lunchtime letters

parts.note: a chunk is a lump
lunchtime is 1 pm, written with the numeral as I to give IPM

explanation.surface: A heavy fellow takes a lunch break, being someone who loves stuffing himself.
explanation.walkthrough: The digit 1 becomes the letter I, a common crossword trick, so 1 PM gives IPM.
explanation.definitionFit: This rodent crams food into its cheek pouches, literally filling its face, a playful description.

clue.text: See business routinely being as regular as this?

parts.note: to clock is informal for to notice or see
routine business is work

explanation.surface: Seeing to business routinely means being as reliable as this.
explanation.walkthrough: 'being' is a link word; the definition alludes to the phrase 'like clockwork', meaning perfectly regular.
explanation.definitionFit: A mechanism driven by springs and gears runs with complete regularity, the model of steady repetition.

clue.text: Buffet with beer

definitions.meaning: to buffet is to strike or batter hard
a colloquial British word for ale or beer

explanation.walkthrough: 'Buffet' looks like a spread of food, but it is the verb to hit.
explanation.definitionFit: A hard blow is a buffet, and the same slang word is used in Britain for beer.

clue.text: This gets carelessly misplaced — perhaps too carelessly

indicators.note: letters treated carelessly are thrown about, so the two words before are rearranged

explanation.surface: A remark that something is often put in the wrong place, maybe too casually.
explanation.walkthrough: The definition plays on the greengrocer's apostrophe, so often put where it does not belong.
explanation.definitionFit: This punctuation mark is notoriously put in the wrong place, as in shop signs selling apple's.

clue.text: One could make strides with this drill possibly

definitions.text: One could make strides with this
definitions.meaning: strides is slang for trousers, so this is cloth for making them
drill is a strong twill cotton, one kind of trouser cloth

explanation.walkthrough: 'strides' looks like walking steps but is slang for trousers, and 'drill' is a fabric, not exercise.
explanation.definitionFit: Trouser cloth is fabric made for legwear, and drill is a twill cotton used that way.

clue.text: Ashmolean regularly reviewed charitable donations

indicators.note: reviewed is read as re-viewed backwards, so the picked letters run in reverse
taking letters at regular intervals means every other letter of the museum's name

explanation.surface: The Oxford museum's gifts from benefactors were inspected again and again.
explanation.walkthrough: The even letters of ASHMOLEAN are S, M, L, A; 'reviewed' reverses them. The Ashmolean is a museum in Oxford.
explanation.definitionFit: Alms are gifts of money or food to the poor, which is exactly charitable donations.

clue.text: Are they boring to do this pop trios like?

definitions.text: Are they boring to do this

indicators.note: letters that pop burst apart and land in a new order

explanation.surface: A question whether pop groups of three enjoy being dull.
explanation.walkthrough: 'boring' looks like dull, but it means drilling; 'pop' is the anagram signal, not music.
explanation.definitionFit: Drillers bore into the ground hoping to find petroleum, so drilling is what they do to find it.

clue.text: Reluctant air settled over gigolo

parts.note: loth means unwilling or reluctant

indicators.note: settled suggests the letters have come to rest in a new arrangement

parts.note: O is the cricket scoring abbreviation for an over

explanation.surface: An unwilling atmosphere hangs over a hired male escort.
explanation.walkthrough: 'settled' rearranges AIR to ARI.
explanation.definitionFit: A lothario is a seducer of women, close to a gigolo as a ladies' man.

clue.text: Stalks cut back in downward spiral

parts.note: to tail someone is to follow or stalk them

indicators.note: back means the word for cut is read in reverse

parts.note: to nip is to cut or pinch off

explanation.surface: Plant stems trimmed back, caught up in a falling twirl.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Stalks' looks like plant stems, but it is the verb to follow, and 'cut' is the verb to nip.
explanation.definitionFit: A tailspin is an aircraft's spinning dive, so figuratively a rapid downward spiral.

clue.text: Detective stifled by a town's bitterness

indicators.note: something stifled is smothered, so the detective sits inside the town

parts.note: a city is a large town
DI is a detective inspector

explanation.surface: An investigator is suffocated by the bitter mood of a place.
explanation.definitionFit: Acidity is sourness or sharpness, as is bitterness in taste or temper.

clue.text: Mike interrupting garbled patois that's laid on thick

indicators.note: interrupting means breaking into, so one letter goes inside the others
garbled speech is mixed up, so the letters of the dialect word are rearranged

parts.note: Mike is the NATO alphabet word for M

explanation.surface: Someone called Mike cuts into muddled dialect that is overdone.
explanation.walkthrough: 'garbled' rearranges PATOIS to IPASTO, and 'interrupting' puts M after the I.
explanation.definitionFit: Impasto is paint applied thickly to a canvas so that it stands up in ridges.

clue.text: All right to uncork wine?

indicators.note: uncorking removes the top, so the first letter of the wine comes off

parts.note: Tokay is a sweet Hungarian wine

explanation.surface: Asking whether it is acceptable to open the wine.
explanation.walkthrough: Tokay is the crossword's favourite Hungarian wine; taking its top off leaves the answer.
explanation.definitionFit: Okay is a casual way of saying all right or acceptable.

clue.text: Generous care of two French gentlemen provoking hatred

parts.note: c/o, CO, is the abbreviation for care of on letters
MM is short for messieurs, French gentlemen
odious means hateful

explanation.surface: Two Frenchmen being kind somehow stir up loathing.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Generous' means roomy here, as in a generous helping.
explanation.definitionFit: Commodious means roomy, and generous can mean ample or spacious, as in generous proportions.

clue.text: Twerps docked point — or lots

indicators.note: docked means cut short, so a letter is removed

parts.note: noodles is slang for foolish people
N is a compass point, north

explanation.surface: Idiots lose a point, or perhaps a great many.
explanation.definitionFit: Oodles is informal for a great quantity, the same as lots.

clue.text: Breathe without sound

parts.note: ex means without, as in ex dividend
hale means healthy or sound

explanation.surface: Breathing without making a noise.
explanation.walkthrough: 'sound' looks like noise, but it means healthy.
explanation.definitionFit: To exhale is to breathe out, one half of breathing.

clue.text: Individually do something with no chance of success

definitions.text: something with no chance of success

parts.note: split into single letters, do gives D and O; D abbreviates dead and O is a duck, a nought in cricket

explanation.surface: Doing a task on one's own that is bound to fail.
explanation.walkthrough: This looks like a plain cryptic definition, but the letters D and O stand for the two words of the answer.
explanation.definitionFit: A failed or hopeless venture is called by this idiom, meaning a plan that cannot succeed.

clue.text: 'Three Men In A Boat' perhaps vaunted

definitions.meaning: the men aboard a boat are its team of sailors or rowers
vaunted means boasted, the old past tense of crow

explanation.walkthrough: Three Men in a Boat is Jerome K Jerome's comic novel of a Thames trip.
explanation.definitionFit: A boat's company is its team, and an old past tense of crow means boasted.

clue.text: Putrid concoction stored originally inside hamper

indicators.note: inside places that letter within the rearranged letters
a concoction is a mixture, so the letters of putrid are mixed up
originally points to the first letter of the word stored

explanation.surface: A rotten mixture has been packed inside a picnic basket.
explanation.walkthrough: 'concoction' rearranges PUTRID to DIRUPT, and 'inside' puts the S in after its first two letters.
explanation.definitionFit: To disrupt is to interfere with, and hamper means to hinder or obstruct.

clue.text: Volunteers not drinking before start of dinner, getting ragged

parts.note: the TA, Territorial Army, is Britain's volunteer reserve force
TT is teetotal
ere means before

indicators.note: the start of a word is its first letter

explanation.surface: Reservists stay sober before dinner yet still look scruffy.
explanation.walkthrough: The TA is the Territorial Army, Britain's part-time volunteer reserve.
explanation.definitionFit: Tattered means torn and worn, so ragged clothes are tattered.

clue.text: A good eighteen holes wrecked

parts.note: a round of golf is eighteen holes

explanation.surface: A good round of golf ends in disaster.
explanation.walkthrough: 'wrecked' looks like ruined; it means a ship stuck on rocks.
explanation.definitionFit: A wrecked ship has run onto the shore or rocks and is stuck fast.
